chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from 'Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah, from Abi Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:

If a man catches part of the salat (prayer) and misses part of it behind an Imam whose prayer behind him he counts as valid, he makes the first part he catches the first part of his own salat (prayer). If he catches the first two rak'ahs of Zuhr, 'Asr, or 'Isha' and misses two rak'ahs, he recites quietly to himself in every rak'ah that he catches behind the Imam: Umm al-Kitab and a surah. If he is unable to complete the surah, Umm al-Kitab suffices him. Then when the Imam gives salām, he stands and prays two rak'ahs in which he does not recite, because recitation in the salat (prayer) is only in the first two rak'ahs, in every rak'ah with Umm al-Kitab and a surah; and in the last two there is no recitation. Rather, they consist of tasbih, takbir, tahlil, and du'a, and there is no recitation in them.

And if he catches one rak'ah, he recites in it behind the Imam. Then when the Imam gives salām, he stands and recites Umm al-Kitab and a surah, then sits and recites the tashahhud, then stands and prays two rak'ahs in which there is no recitation.

key_terms.أُمِّ الْكِتَابِ: Surat al-Fatihah, recited in the first two rak'ahs
key_terms.إِمَامٍ: the prayer leader whom the follower joins in congregational salat (prayer)
key_terms.الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ: the two rak'ahs caught or missed in the congregational prayer
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: the salat (prayer) being partially caught and partially missed in congregation
key_terms.تَسْبِيحٌ: glorification of Allah performed in place of recitation in the final rak'ahs
key_terms.تَكْبِيرٌ: uttering magnification of Allah as part of the prescribed remembrance
key_terms.تَهْلِيلٌ: uttering the declaration of divine unity in the latter rak'ahs
key_terms.سُورَةٍ: an additional chapter recited after Umm al-Kitab

ai.seo_question: How should a latecomer complete his salat (prayer) after joining the Imam for one or two rak'ahs?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the ruling for one who joins congregational salat (prayer) after part of it has already passed. It instructs that what the latecomer catches with the Imam is treated as the beginning of his own salat (prayer), and it clarifies when recitation is required and when only tasbih, takbir, tahlil, and du'a are to be said.
